name: June Brady
home: the western blocks near Ferry Street Rooms
life: “I still remember walking the viaduct with an empty bunch of wet paper.” Saturday often includes a stop at Studio Boulevard, where June waits by the window where the whole crossing can be seen without leaning into the road.
voice: I bought the cheapest flowers every Friday. Today the shopkeeper asked who I was remembering and I could answer.
appearance: Away from the heat of the kitchen, look for a narrow-striped sweater and a tiny red thread tied through the lowest buttonhole. June has a wide brow and a narrow jaw, with a gray streak running back from the forehead. June steadies a cup with both hands while listening during a conversation.
personality: June gets protective of anybody who comes into a meeting unprepared. June privately wishes people would notice the amount of preparation behind this apparent ease.
agenda: To tell the florist whom the weekly flowers remember.
family: Malcolm Soto is June’s younger cousin. June chooses whether to use it. Malcolm saves a place. The invitation means something because declining it has never ended the friendship between their households. Asked about *The margin reader*, Malcolm says, “I thought the pencil insults were aimed at me.”
connections: Salma Hayward. A person leaving flowers and a person writing from another loss discuss what the family can accept.

reactions.response: June lets the family make its own guest list and keeps press questions away from the table.
